task_spec: SUBJECT: Let a conflict resolution name the record that wins, so an operator merging from more than one source collection can say WHICH source supplies a track's values, instead of a base|source token that silently resolves to whichever source keep-first names.

SETTLED by the operator: a resolution maps an identity key to the winning record's primary key rather than to the token 'base' or 'source'. One vocabulary covers base-vs-source, source-vs-source, and a group holding no base record.

SETTLED by the operator: the bulk actions become All base plus one action per source collection, named for that collection, each settling every group that collection holds a record in. They currently read All base / All source.

scope: traktor_nml/splice.py (_resolve_conflicts' resolution branch, ConflictRow, the entry-patch path), traktor_nml/gui/conflict_model.py (the decision states, the row projection, the bulk resolution, the resolutions mapping), traktor_nml/gui/app.py (the conflict rows and the bulk controls on the reconstruct page), design/reconnect-wizard/Specs.dc.html, tests/, traktor_nml/README.md, and the gate repository's reconstruct fixture
out-of-scope: accessibility work - no screen-reader verification, no NVDA, no new keyboard bindings. Mouse and clicking is this version's bar
out-of-scope: the reconnect wizard's own four steps and its review table
out-of-scope: the run-wide --on-conflict keep-first|keep-last CLI flag, which stays as it is and keeps governing groups no resolution names (DL-108)
out-of-scope: the quadratic replacement-application loop in assemble_output, which is a separate known finding
constraints: MUST: ConflictRow's identity_key, attrs and resolution fields keep their current meaning - traktor_nml/commands/splice_cmd.py's _write_conflict_report writes exactly those three as the conflict report's CSV columns, and the CLI is not changing

MUST: the resolutions mapping's values change vocabulary, so every caller and guard naming 'base' or 'source' as a mapping VALUE is enumerated and updated; the operator-facing words base and source may remain as labels
MUST: a resolution naming a record that is not a member of that group is inert rather than an error, the way an unmatched identity key already is (DL-105)
MUST: DL-115's re-attachment rule still holds - a held pick re-attaches only where the group's member primary keys are the identical set - and its guards pass unchanged
MUST: DL-116 still holds - a pick that names a base record keeps base's own ENTRY and rewrites only the divergent attribute values; the merged COLLECTION holds at most one entry per LOCATION (DL-004)
MUST: the nicegui boundary (DL-069) - conflict_model.py imports no nicegui; app.py, file_picker.py and __main__.py are the only three that may
MUST: app.py stays 100% CRLF (1636 CRLF, 0 bare LF); splice.py, conflict_model.py and the tests are LF. Read and write with newline=''
MUST: every guard is made to FAIL first, and its docstring records the specific mutation applied and the specific output observed
MUST: a served-page gate run before the change lands, over a fixture carrying at least two source collections that disagree with each other and with base (DL-084, DL-113)
MUST: new decisions continue from the current high-water mark in traktor_nml/README.md - re-read and confirm it rather than assuming
MUST: documentation describes the code as it stands - no 'previously', 'now does', 'no longer', 'added'
MUST NOT: regenerate the parity manifest or the gate fixture under fixture/w002gatefix2; never restore a file with git checkout
SHOULD: the suite runs under the SYSTEM interpreter, currently 503 passed / 3 skipped, not .venv

rejected_alternatives: Keep base|source and refuse what it cannot express - the page would name the disagreeing sources and refuse to settle the group. Rejected by the operator: it makes the defect visible without letting them choose
Leave it and record it in the decision log and TODO.md - rejected by the operator; the wrong value still gets written silently on a multi-source run
Keep base|source and add a second run-wide flag naming which source wins - a run-wide answer to a per-track question, which is the shape the per-key mapping already replaced
Bulk actions reduced to All base and All first source - rejected by the operator in favour of one action per source collection
Drop bulk actions on multi-source runs - rejected by the operator; a large conflict set would become per-row work
current_understanding: measured today, base plus two sources disagreeing three ways on BITRATE: the row's source_values reads (('064', '128'),), the page displays '064 / 128', and a 'source' resolution applies {'bitrate': '128'} - keep-first's answer - with no way for the operator to choose 064
the join with ' / ' exists in conflict_model precisely because the pick the operator is asked for cannot express which source, so the display had to collapse several answers into one cell

pick_non_base() serves two different questions: which non-base copy survives when no base record exists, and which non-base record supplies a source pick's values. Only the second is wrong; the first is the run-wide policy doing its job

the review also claimed a group holding NO base record accepts a pick the core ignores. I tried to reproduce it and did not - my fixture still grouped base into the set - so that half is UNVERIFIED and the plan should establish it by reading rather than repeat it
resolutions values are currently the literals 'base' and 'source'; splice compares `resolution == 'source'` and conflict_model's BASE/SOURCE constants carry the same two strings
ConflictRow already carries member_keys, so the members' primary keys are already in the row - what is missing is which value belongs to which record
assumptions: The row needs one option per distinct candidate record, each with its own values, rather than two sides - the plan should settle the shape (M)

A group holding several base records already redirects to base_members[0] and keeps its non-base keys ambiguous (DL-122); a resolution naming one of those non-base records interacts with that rule and the plan must say how (M)
Two sources that agree with each other but differ from base should still present as one option rather than two identical ones (M)
The bulk action per source collection needs a label; the page holds the source paths, so the file name is available (H)
invisible_knowledge: A SOURCE pick keeps base's ENTRY and rewrites the divergent attribute values inside it, because transplanting the source's ENTRY produced two COLLECTION entries sharing one LOCATION, which DL-004 forbids - the defect a served-page gate run caught after a green suite
Serving the page is the only gate that has ever caught a defect in gui/ (DL-084)

A guard asserting the right value appeared can pass while the output is wrong - assert the count, the structure, or the thing the defect would change. Nine guards were green while the output held two entries for one file

conflict_groups projects a group from a ConflictRow alone and takes no records and no MatchConfidence; the page and the core agree because the core reports what it grouped rather than the page regrouping
old_to_new_key holds only keys a resolution actually redirected; a key with no mapping passes through as the raw key rather than erroring (DL-101)
The primary key is derived from the location, so two entries for one file cannot be told apart by key
Quasar's no-outline carries outline:0 !important inside a layer the page orders last; an unlayered add_head_html rule loses at every specificity (DL-086's ladder)
A token class carrying background and ink together needs color=None at the constructor
